sophia.k: Hey — bringing up qwen-3-small-v2 on the infra runner and seeing weird token/id misalignments. Generation sometimes starts with random ASCII chars and eval loss spikes vs qwen-base. Anyone seen tokenizer offset issues across qwen/mistral/llama families?

jonah: hmm, any concrete repro? sample input + token ids?

sophia.k: repro attached below (quick):
```
# quick check
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('qwen/qwen-3-small-v2')
print(t.encode('Hello world'))
# got: [1543, 998, 27, 2] but runtime model expects ids around 100000+ for same subwords
```

alisa: that sounds like a vocab id offset. qwen variants sometimes publish tokenizers with different id mapping for shared merges. Could be our loader applying an extra offset when converting to the runtime vocab.

matt: also check rotary params — last time mismatched rotary base (10000 vs 4096 scaled) caused attention drift which looked like tokenization noise in early tokens. Are we using the model-provided rotary configs or forcing a runtime default?

jonah: good call. If the model's config has `rotary_emb.scale` or `rotary_base` fields we should honor them. Our quantized kernels assume rotary_dim layout = head_dim, so mismatch can produce weird logits.

eva: quick automation note: ci-bot ran the compile job on that commit and failed later in generation tests. logs had this snippet: `RuntimeWarning: token id 12345 not in embedding table (size 32768)`

max: that's the exact indicator of an id offset. Two common causes we've seen: 1) tokenizer with added BOS/EOS pseudo tokens shifting ids, 2) tokenizer/vocab produced by a different tokenizer library (sentencepiece vs tokenizer) and we map incorrectly.

sophia.k: I dug in — qwen tokenizer has `special_tokens_map` that includes `<s>` and `</s>` with ids 0/1, but the model's hf-weights expect `<s>` at 100000. So looks like an off-by-vocab (hf->runtime) mapping during our conversion step.

alisa: action: write a small mapping shim that remaps the tokenizer ids to model embedding indices when converting. e.g. 
```
# mapping pseudo
new_ids = [model_vocab_index[t] for t in hf_token_ids]
```
Make it opt-in and add a CI check comparing first 512 token ids on a small seed set.

matt: on rotary: I'm going to add a sanity check that compares rotary proj matrix shapes and base params between checkpoint config and runtime kernel config. If mismatch, fail fast with an explanatory message.

jonah: also add an eval smoke: run a short perplexity check on the first 256 tokens of WikiText. If perplexity jumps > 1.5x vs expected, block the roll. That will catch both token mapping and attention/rotary mismatches.

eva: about quant: I ran nf4/int8 quantization on qwen and saw token-level logit noise when using fused attention kernels vs interpreter kernels. So for onboarding, we should compare generation outputs FP32 vs quantized for a few prompts and measure KL divergence over softmaxes.

max: yes — quantization can amplify token misalignments. Also note that some models use rotated token embeddings (rotary scaling) which are sensitive to low-bit rounding. Adding a tiny calibration pass (1000 tokens) for rotary parameters in quant conversion helped us before.

ci-bot: nightly-build #2762 started for branch model-onboard/qwen-interop — tests: tokenizer-mapping, rotary-sanity, perplexity-smoke.

alisa: next steps:
- sophia: run token mapping shim + rerun generation smoke (ETA today)
- matt: add rotary config mismatch check + unit test (ETA tomorrow)
- jonah: add perplexity blocker in onboard pipeline + KL check for quantized vs fp32 (ETA 48h)
- eva/max: run nf4/int8 calibration experiments and post a short table of KL/perp impact

sophia.k: I will also dump the tokenizer vocab head/tail sample and share — weirdly qwen's vocab ordering differs for CJK tokens so may need special-case mapping.

jonah: thanks. If anyone finds a case where token ids are in-range but embeddings still mismatch, look for endian issues in weight serialization (we had a stray endian swap bug last year).

matt: logging a short RFC in #eng-ml-docs: "onboarding checklist: tokenizer id mapping, rotary param validation, quant KL test, perp smoke" — will link once posted.

sophia.k: great, thanks all. will update thread when regen runs finish. :thumbsup:
